claims.text: A nanocrystalline AlCoCrFeNi-based HEA coating can be deposited onto a copper substrate.
The AlCoCrFeNi-based coating will adhere strongly to the copper substrate.
The resulting AlCoCrFeNi-based surface layer will be ultrahard.
The HEA coating will significantly reduce wear relative to uncoated copper.
Minor Ti additions can further promote formation of protective oxides.
Sputtering can produce the proposed AlCoCrFeNi-based thin film on copper.
Spark-plasma-sintering-assisted deposition can produce the proposed thin film on copper.
The deposited coating will have a refined nanocrystalline microstructure.
During service, the coating will develop a continuous protective oxide layer containing Al2O3, Cr2O3, or spinel phases.
Severe lattice distortion in the HEA promotes high hardness.
Mechanical action induces tribo-oxidation of the HEA coating.
The tribologically formed oxide film reduces abrasion and improves wear resistance.
A favorable coating microstructure helps ensure strong adhesion to copper.
Relatively compatible thermal expansion between the coating and copper helps ensure strong adhesion.
The coated copper will have greater surface hardness than bare copper.
The coating will not delaminate prematurely during wear testing.
Bare copper has low hardness and a high wear rate in tribological applications.
Extreme thermal cycling or very high temperatures may compromise coating adhesion.
Thermal-expansion mismatch and interdiffusion at the coating–copper interface could impair performance.

contradictions.description: The mechanism invokes relatively compatible thermal expansion as a source of strong adhesion, whereas the uncertainty field invokes thermal-expansion mismatch as a possible source of poor performance; the degree and direction of compatibility are not resolved.
